Welcome

Clif Notes

Build it · Print it · Share it · Everything stays on your device
The basics

Add: Shapes tab → tap any shape. It drops on the plate, already selected.

Move: drag a selected object with one finger. Empty space drags the camera. Pinch zooms.

Edit: tap an object → bottom panel: size, rotate, lift, color.

Sketch mode (draw → solid)

Shapes tab → Draw. Camera flips to a top-down blueprint view. Tap to place points — each line shows its live length in mm and snaps straight to 0°/45°/90° (toggle Straight off for free angles).

Drag any point to fine-tune it. Tap the white first point or hit Finish to close the outline, pick a wall height, and it becomes a solid part — custom brackets, odd-shaped plates, anything the basic shapes can't make. Don't let lines cross each other.

Holes & engraving (the bracket-maker)

Select a shape → Make hole. It turns translucent orange. Push it into a solid where you want material removed. On STL export, holes are truly cut out — screw holes, slots, channels.

Engraving trick: add Text, mark it as a hole, sink it slightly into a plate. Exported part has recessed lettering.

Hole rule of thumb: make the hole taller than the part it cuts through so it punches all the way.

Groups / assemblies

Edit tab → Multi → tap each piece → Group. The assembly now moves, rotates, and scales as one unit. Ungroup breaks it apart again.

Text

Shapes tab → Text → type a label (A–Z, 0–9). Solid text on top of a part = raised embossing. Hole text = engraving.

Comic Studio (photos → comic strips)

Tap the Comic pill in the ribbon. Snap or upload a photo and it gets comic-inked on your phone — bold outlines and poster colors, three styles: Pop (color), Ink (black & white), Sketch (line art). Pick the style before adding the photo.

Tap a panel to select it, then add characters, speech bubbles, and caption boxes. Drag anything to place it, pinch to size it. The ⇄ button flips a bubble's tail, ⬆ brings an item to the front.

PNG exports the finished strip ready to share or print. Save keeps the whole comic as a file you can reload and keep working on.

Skit Studio (animate your characters)

Tap Skit in the ribbon (or 🎬 from the comic). Cast shows every character you've already inked in your comic chapters — tap one to put them on stage, or shoot a new photo.

The animation trick is one move: scrub the timeline, then drag your actor. Every drag records a keyframe (the gold diamonds). Scrub ahead, drag again, press play — they travel between poses. Pinch or +/− to grow and shrink (that gets keyframed too). ⇄ mirrors an actor to face the other way.

Bubbles appear at the moment on the timeline where you add them and pop away after their duration (⏲ cycles 1.5s–6s). 🎥 Video plays the skit once and records it into a real .webm video file you can text or post. The skit saves inside the same team project file.

Team comics (sign in · chapters · log)

When Comic Studio opens, sign in with your name (tap the round chip up top to switch people). Everything anyone adds is recorded in the Log — who did what, in which chapter, and when.

Chapters hold the story: add new ones, rename them, and jump between them. Inside a chapter, use + Before / + After to insert panels at any point in the strip and − Remove to cut one — up to 9 panels per chapter.

Working as a team: the comic autosaves on this device. Hit Save to write the whole project (all chapters, pictures, and the log) to one file — text it or share it to a teammate, they Load it, sign in with their name, add their part, save, and pass it on. The log keeps everyone's credits.

Float Builder (parade floats, in inches)

Tap the Float pill. You get a 3D trailer hitched to a full-size long-bed pickup, already dressed with the Pack 101 layout: glacier with signs and emblems, campfire, lake with the kayak, docks and waves, and scouts in the truck bed.

Add anything from the library, tap a piece to select it, drag it to move. The Selected panel takes exact numbers: inches from the deck front, inches off centerline, rotation and size. It also shows the gap to each rail.

Trailer & truck holds every rig dimension. Change the deck length and the float, the checks and the parts list all follow. Top and Side views are true to scale; deck grid = 1 ft.

Checks flag overhang, height, width, payload and riders vs seats. Parts list is Have / Buy / Make with rough costs and a CSV export. Plan has the renders, rib profiles, wave and flame patterns, and the cut list.

Tour walks the build in ten steps; How-to video records that tour to a video file you can text to den leaders. Save downloads a layout file the pack passes around, same as comic projects.

4D mode (the time dimension)

4D printing is real technology: parts printed in smart materials (shape-memory polymers, hydrogels) that transform after printing when triggered by heat, water, or light — flat-pack parts that fold themselves, pipes that expand, grippers that close.

Flip the 4D pill in the ribbon. Select a part → Set start → move/rotate/resize it → Set end. Scrub the timeline or press play — every keyed part morphs between its two states. Pick the trigger (🔥 💧 ☀️) your material responds to.

Design rule: 0% is what you print, 100% is what it becomes. Export STL at 0% for the printable file. Tap Demo 4D for a heat-activated bloom.

From screen to plastic — the print pipeline
1Design here. The grid is your print bed: 1 square = 10 mm. The 18×18 plate ≈ a standard 180 mm printer bed.
2Export → STL. STL is the universal 3D print format — a mesh of triangles describing your part's surface. Holes are subtracted during export.
3Open the STL in a free slicer (Cura or PrusaSlicer). It cuts the model into layers and makes G-code — the printer's instruction language. Pick material and layer height here.
4Load G-code on the printer and go. First layer is everything — keep big flat faces on the bed.
Pro tips

• Snap (Edit tab) locks moves to half-grid steps — great for lining up screw holes.

• Top view (View tab) is the layout view — design like you're reading a blueprint.

• Save file often. Designs save as JSON you can reload, share, or text to someone.

• Overhangs droop when printed. Wedges and cones print cleaner than mushroom shapes.

    Build order

    StepWorkWhy this order
    1Chalk the deck outline full size on the driveway; set the kayak, benches and ring inside itSettles fit before anything is cut
    2Turf on 0–98″, blue floor on 98″–rear, wave sills screwed downEverything else sits on top
    3Glacier ribs + base + stringers; screw base to deckBiggest piece, sets the height
    4Skin, carve and paint the glacier; mount the sign facesFoam dust and paint before riders' seating goes in
    5Fire base disc, blocks glued, plenum, duct to the blower inside the glacierDuct runs under the turf
    6Dock boxes, pilings, rope; kayak saddles and strapsSeating locked down
    7Wave panels (back layer, then front), skirt, trees, signs, emblemsDress last so nothing gets dinged
    8Full rehearsal: load riders, run the blower off the generator, drive the block at parade speedFind the loose stuff before the crowd does
